We need to propose a retrosynthesis route with 3 reactions for target SMILES: Cc1ccc(NS(=O)(=O)c2ccc(/C=C/C(=O)Nc3ccccc3N)cc2)cc1

We have guidance: step 1 (forward) is amide formation from carboxylic acid + amine (coupling). So retrosynthetic step: break amide bond to give carboxylic acid and amine.

Step 2: Doebner modification: aromatic aldehyde + malonic acid -> α,β-unsaturated carboxylic acid (the double bond). In our target, we have /C=C/C(=O)N... So the unsaturated acid is part of the chain: aromatic ring (c2ccc(... )cc2) attached to C=C-CO-N... The unsaturated acid likely derived from aldehyde on that aromatic ring (c2ccc(CHO)cc2) reacting with malonic acid to give the α,β-unsaturated acid (c2ccc(/C=C/COOH)cc2). Then later amide formation attaches the aniline (Nc3ccccc3N) to the acid.

Step 3: Sulfonamide formation: aniline (the first aromatic ring with methyl) reacts with sulfonyl chloride (maybe p-toluenesulfonyl chloride) to give sulfonamide linking to second aromatic sulfonyl group? Actually target has NS(=O)(=O) attached to second aromatic ring. So sulfonamide formation between aniline (first ring) and sulfonyl chloride derived from second aromatic sulfonyl group (p-toluenesulfonyl chloride). So retrosynthetic step: break S-N bond to give aniline and aryl sulfonyl chloride.

Thus three steps: 1) amide formation (break amide). 2) Doebner modification (break C=C double bond and carboxyl). 3) sulfonamide formation (break S-N).

We need to produce JSON tree: root molecule, then children reaction nodes each with template_id (we need actual IDs). We can search for templates for amide formation, Doebner modification, sulfonamide formation.

Search for amide formation template (break amide). Use search with functional_groups_broken: amide.
